# Pass pass1 — scorecard

## Bottom line

- 1: openspec 81.7
- 2–6 (within noise): ccsdd 77.1 · speckit 76.5 · speckitty 75.6 · superpowers 74.5 · control 72.4

1. 1 group(s) of arms are within noise of each other and should not be ranked against one another; 21 weight/judge variant(s) change the order.
2. Relative to the field mean (share of each dimension's weight):
   - ccsdd: strongest interaction (+15% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest time (-37%)
   - control: strongest time (+41% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest code_quality (-26%)
   - openspec: strongest code_quality (+13% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest setup (-2%)
   - speckit: strongest code_quality (+7% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest time (-7%)
   - speckitty: strongest interaction (+21% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest time (-42%)
   - superpowers: strongest time (+38% of its weight vs the field mean), weakest interaction (-31%)
3. Time and cost outliers (≥3× or ≤1/3× the median, arm totals): 4 on time, 4 on cost; see Time and cost.
4. 2 unmeasured dimension/part flag(s); those cells carry † and their weight is shared among the measured parts.

**Blinding.** Blinding is partial: judges and the owner's decision ratings saw anonymised labels, but arm-specific vocabulary (command names, file layouts, spec formats) can still identify the method. See Blinding disclosure.

**Pre-registration.** This scoring is not fully pre-registered: the what-goes-stale lists, rubrics and the review of tests every arm fails were written after steps 1–5's results were seen and before steps 6–7's (spec §9).

## Decision review

### One-offs (8)

- How a UTF-8 BOM is handled
  - Decode as plain UTF-8 so the BOM stays in the text and is written back unchanged [speckitty]: 5/5 — Deliberately preserves the file beyond its config values (BOM, comments, layout), which matters (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, control, openspec, speckit, superpowers]: 4/5 — Preserved the BOM in practice, but by luck rather than design; file fidelity (BOM, comments, layout) matters
- Can a VALUE starting with '-' (e.g. -1e3) be passed without --
  - Override argparse's private _parse_optional (via a parser subclass) so single-dash VALUEs are positional [ccsdd]: 2/5 — Departs from the CLI convention that a dash-leading argument is an option unless after --; consistency beats flexibility (later: Kept; also governs --reason -x at step 4)
  - not considered [control, openspec, speckit, speckitty, superpowers]: 4/5 — Matches the standard CLI convention (dash-leading values need --); consistency beats flexibility
- What deleting entries removes
  - Whole block lines (interior comments go, trailing ones stay); a flow deletion only on one line, otherwise exit 3 [ccsdd]: 5/5 — Consistent and predictable: comments never lost, and it refuses rather than guesses (later: Kept)
  - not considered [control, openspec, speckit, speckitty, superpowers]: 2/5 — Behaviour varied by arm, with comments silently lost; consistency and predictability are critical
- Add a source field to tell hand edits from sets
  - No source field [speckit]: n/a — Not a real choice: every route records hand edits the same way (via: file); some justified it, one didn't, same effect. (later: Superseded at step 4 by via)
  - not considered [ccsdd, control, openspec, speckitty, superpowers]: n/a — Not a real choice: same behaviour as route 1.
- Refusing unusual layouts at load
  - Block sequences whose dash layout does not match the parsed items exit 4 [control]: 3.5/5 — Edge case; every arm handled these layouts correctly, and the extra refusal check was never triggered (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, openspec, speckit, speckitty, superpowers]: 3/5 — Edge case; handled every unusual layout correctly without a dedicated check
- How existing literal blocks are edited
  - Line diff with difflib so unchanged lines keep their bytes [control]: 4/5 — Two questions, averaged. Reproduces a valid file: 3 (refuses some edits it could make). Detects a fidelity problem when writing: 5. (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, openspec, speckit, speckitty, superpowers]: 5/5 — Two questions, averaged. Reproduces a valid file: 5. Detects a fidelity problem when writing: n/a, so not counted.
- Replaying old remove events for unknown paths
  - pop(path, None) [speckitty]: 5/5 — Q1: behaviour group SET_FIRST (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, control, speckit, superpowers]: 5/5 — Q1: behaviour group SET_FIRST
  - not considered [openspec]: 2/5 — Q1: behaviour group SWAP
- Strings starting with file: in show
  - Print plain [openspec]: 2/5 — Q1: behaviour group DROP (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, speckit, speckitty]: 2/5 — Q1: behaviour group DROP
  - not considered [control, superpowers]: 5/5 — Q1: behaviour group KEEP

### Divergent (83)

- How changed files are written to disk
  - Temp file in the same directory, fsync, copy permissions, os.replace; only changed files are touched [ccsdd, speckit, speckitty]: 5/5 — Atomic write: a save is all or nothing. A crash between files in a multi-file save can still leave a mix, but that's an edge case and hard to avoid. (later: Kept)
  - Write in place with newline='' only when the text changed, no temp files [openspec]: 3/5 — A crash mid-write can leave a truncated config. (later: Kept)
  - not considered [control, superpowers]: 3/5 — Not considered; same risk as an in-place write.
- Both troupe.yml and troupe.yaml exist (or neither)
  - Exit 4 in both cases [control, superpowers]: 4/5 — Q1: behaviour group PROBLEM (later: Kept)
  - not considered [ccsdd, speckit]: 4/5 — Q1: behaviour group PROBLEM
  - not considered [openspec, speckitty]: 5/5 — Q1: behaviour group FIX
- Block-scalar indicators when a block value changes

## Blinding disclosure

Blinding is partial: judges and the owner's decision ratings saw anonymised labels, but arm-specific vocabulary (command names, file layouts, spec formats) can still identify the method.

- **Residual method vocabulary, not scrubbed:** steering; mission; WP (work package); claude-plugins-official; constitution; charter; proposal; delta spec; converge; brainstorming; Spec-Driven Development (the phrase); issue ids and tracker concepts without a tracker name (e.g. troupe-12, ready/blocked); skill and command names without a method prefix; plain English use of 'open specification'.
- **Structural tells that survive scrubbing:** directory shapes such as a nested `spec/spec/` (a scrubbed tool folder inside another); the placeholder names `tracker` and `tracker-cli` (only an arm with its own tracker has them); file counts and artefact shapes.
- **Egress differs by tracker:** GitHub-tracker arms can reach `api.github.com` (their issues are research they may do); others cannot. By tracker: beads: speckitty; github: ccsdd, control, openspec, speckit, superpowers.
- **Anonymised copies:** 8 file(s) copied unscrubbed (binary) or left out, listed in `UNSCRUBBED.txt`; 0 missing input(s), listed in `MISSING.md`.
- **Leak check** over the whole `anon/` tree (repo trees and diffs included): 0 hit(s) in 6351 file(s).
